sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.1 model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: exact v25.08 card identifies mistral-medium-2508, August 12, 2025, Premier status, nominal 128k context, text/image input and text output tooltips, function calling and document QnA. The card is deprecated and identifies Medium 3.5 as its replacement; no parameter count is given.

sources.title: Mistral documentation model data: exact Medium 3.1 object
sources.evidence: The object named Mistral Medium 3.1 has slug mistral-medium-3-1-25-08, API identifier mistral-medium-2508, type Premier, an empty weights array, contextLength 128k, input text/image, output text, and function-calling/document-qna features. It has no parameter or architecture specification. It records deprecation 2026-05-22 and retirement 2026-08-31.

sources.title: Mistral changelog: August 12, 2025
sources.evidence: Explicitly records the release of Mistral Medium 3.1, mistral-medium-2508, on August 12 in the 2025 chronology, separately from Medium 3 in May 2025 and Medium 3.5 in April 2026.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3 family legal and lifecycle documentation
sources.evidence: Names Medium 3.1 as an August 12, 2025 update within the Medium 3 model lifecycle. The embedded Technical Documentation content says documentation for 3.0 and subsequent 3.1/3.5 updates is still being prepared. Its Active lifecycle label conflicts with the inference card's deprecation data; it does not establish endpoint operation.

sources.title: Mistral known limitations: context windows
sources.evidence: Lists Medium 3.1 separately from 3.5 with a 128k-token context, including input and output. No token-exact integer is supplied for 3.1.

sources.title: Mistral Document AI QnA
sources.evidence: Explains Document QnA as OCR extraction followed by language-model analysis and shows PDF document_url requests. This distinguishes PDF service support from the model card's native text/image modalities.

sources.title: Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium Technical Report
sources.evidence: Reopened the full May 2026 HTX/Mistral report October 27. The abstract calls Phoenix a 123B-parameter multimodal model continued-pretrained from Mistral Medium 3.1; section 1.1 names that base checkpoint. Section 5.2 preserves the multimodal backbone. Sections 5.3-5.4 describe context extension, full-parameter SFT, teacher-loss distillation, vision freezing/unfreezing and preference training, with no reported pruning, expert expansion or structural compression. Section 3 describes a decoder-only Transformer and 2B vision encoder. This supports a nominal 123B total by named-base lineage, not an exact deployed tensor census. Tables 2-3 label Phoenix only 123B; their A-suffixed active sizes concern other models, and section 5.4.1's 41B active belongs to the Large 3 teacher.

sources.title: Mistral model selection guide with Medium 3.1 query
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the comparison still renders Medium 3.5 despite the Medium 3.1 query. Its explicitly labeled 128B total and 128B active figures belong to Medium 3.5 and do not establish Medium 3.1's counts.

sources.title: Mistral commercial terms of service
sources.evidence: Current commercial terms grant limited product access and reserve Mistral's ownership of its products and underlying model materials. Together with the exact model's Premier classification and absence of distributed weights, this supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not a named open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Mistral Medium 3.1 endpoints
sources.evidence: Exact model ID mistralai/mistral-medium-3.1 has three endpoints explicitly naming provider Mistral, each publishing context_length 131072 and support for tools/tool_choice. This is primary evidence of the serving-provider configuration, not an independent measurement of the native model limit.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the later sibling card identifies Medium 3.1 as a predecessor but reports dense 128B and configurable reasoning for Medium 3.5 only. It describes 3.5's merged model and newly trained vision encoder; those specifications are not transferred to 3.1.

sources.title: Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium: Continued Pre-Training of Sovereign Multimodal AI for On-Premises Public-Sector Deployment
sources.publisher: HTX and Mistral AI; EMNLP 2026 Industry Track
sources.evidence: Read the full October 2026 paper on October 27. Abstract and section 2 give the complete multimodal Phoenix model a nominal 123B size. Section 3.2.1 explicitly identifies base Mistral Medium 3.1, and reference Mistral AI (2025b) specifies Model ID mistral-medium-2508. Table 4 tracks that named base through CPT, SFT, ODPO and domain training. Section 3 and Appendix H describe full-parameter tuning and teacher-loss distillation; Appendix B retains decoder-only GQA, a 2B vision encoder and 131072-token vocabulary. No structural resizing is described. Tables 7-10 label Phoenix 123B without a separate active count; A-suffixed counts apply to comparison models.

sources.title: Heaps do lie: debugging a memory leak in vLLM
sources.evidence: Reopened January 2026 engineering article on October 27 as a later exact-model technical source. It identifies Mistral Medium 3.1 in disaggregated vLLM serving tests and discusses graph-compilation memory leaks, but does not disclose total or active parameter counts. Runtime memory growth is not used to derive model size.

name.note: Exact name and dated API identity match the frozen record.

developer.note: Retains the catalog's normalized label for Mistral AI.

family.note: The developer places 3.1 within the Medium 3 lifecycle.

license.note: Descriptive commercial classification; no specific public weight-license identifier is established.

parameters_b.note: Nominal 123B inferred from the developer-coauthored Phoenix lineage: both reports identify the Medium 3.1 base, and the later paper cites its exact mistral-medium-2508 ID. The documented adaptation preserves the multimodal backbone and describes training rather than structural resizing. This is a labeled lineage inference, not a direct Medium 3.1 tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Still undisclosed after fresh exact-name and dated-ID searches for active/activated counts and later research tables. Phoenix's 123B is a total; neither its May report nor October EMNLP paper states a separate active count. The teacher's 41B active and Medium 3.5's 128B active describe different models, so neither is transferred.

architecture.note: The named-base Phoenix lineage supports a decoder-only Transformer inference, but neither report explicitly establishes dense versus MoE routing for Medium 3.1. The catalog's categorical architecture remains unverified.

context_window.note: Retained as the exact hosted capacity published for Mistral's Medium 3.1 endpoints by OpenRouter. Mistral's native documentation says only nominal 128k; it does not independently establish a token-exact bound.

modalities.note: Remove PDF from native model modalities: the documented PDF QnA service combines OCR preprocessing with model analysis.

reasoning.note: The exact model lists text output and no dedicated reasoning control, but absence is insufficient to verify a categorical false. 3.5's explicit reasoning mode cannot be transferred.

tool_call.note: Exact card and serving endpoints explicitly support function calling.

sources.label: Phoenix-VL exact-base lineage and training stages (EMNLP 2026)

patch.notes: Exact revision: mistral-medium-2508. Total 123B is a nominal lineage inference from the HTX/Mistral Phoenix reports, which identify this base checkpoint and describe continued training with the multimodal backbone preserved. Active parameters and dense versus MoE routing remain undisclosed. Medium 3.5 specifications are not transferred. Context 131072 is OpenRouter's Mistral-provider hosted capacity; Mistral's native card states nominal 128k. Native inputs are text and images; PDF QnA uses OCR preprocessing. No dedicated reasoning mode was verified. The card is deprecated, and model data records retirement on 2026-08-31; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit establishes a nominal 123B total through the HTX/Mistral Phoenix lineage, supported by the October EMNLP paper's exact mistral-medium-2508 reference and staged training history. Active parameters remain undisclosed after separate exact-model searches and comparison-table review; Phoenix totals, Large 3 teacher counts and Medium 3.5 counts are kept distinct. Density/routing remains unverified, with its note corrected to acknowledge the supported Transformer lineage. Other field values and prior corrections are preserved.
